newsitem.title: USA: Man pulls gun on California labor commission.
newsitem.headline: Man pulls gun on California labor commission.

text.p: A man pulled a loaded gun on California labor commissioners Friday at the end of an explosive meeting on changing state overtime rules, officials said.

The man went up to panel members at the end of the state Industrial Welfare Commission's meeting in San Francisco as if to ask a question, but instead pulled the pistol from behind his back, they said.
California Highway Patrol officers quickly subdued the man, later identified as Andrew Barnett, 37, and arrested him, CHP spokesman Shawn Chase said. No shots were fired and nobody was injured.
"He meant business," Chase said. "He was very serious."
"The commission members were shocked. Nothing like that has ever happened at their meetings before," Chase said.
The man drew the gun soon after the commission voted 3-2 to change the state's employee overtime policy from an eight-hour workday standard to a 40-hour workweek standard.

The incident capped an emotional hearing at which labor representatives and other protesters heckled the commissioners. At least three protesters were forcibly removed from the hearing room after the commission's vote.
"It's a very emotional issue," said Rick Rice, deputy director of the state's Department of Industrial Relations. "People look suspiciously at change."
Several of the commissioners had received threatening phone calls at their homes before Friday's meeting, according to a spokesman for California Gov. Pete Wilson.
Under the new rules adopted by the commission, many private-sector workers would only be eligible for overtime once they have worked at least 40 hours in a week.
Under the old rule, a worker became eligible for overtime on a daily basis after putting in eight hours.
